title: Apostolic and Disciple Writings — Unified Historical Collection
ordering: Chronological by estimated composition date; records with undetermined dates appear last. Overlapping ranges are not a claim of exact sequence.
scope: All identifiable writings connected by historical attribution, claim, tradition, subject, or early community use to apostles and disciples, including gospels, letters, testimony, acts, instruction, apocalypses, and other related writings. Inclusion is not an endorsement of authenticity, apostolic authorship, inspiration, or historical accuracy.
anti_compilation_rule: Do not use the later 27-writing compilation as the archive boundary or as the ordering template. Preserve its history as one later classification only.
date_policy: Composition date estimates are stored separately from physical witness dates. Use null for undetermined dates; never use numeric sentinels. Where estimates overlap or are disputed, show a date band and mark sequence as approximate.
evidence_policy: Every entry must distinguish title tradition, actual author identification, date of composition, earliest surviving witness, manuscript text status, and historical reliability. Anonymous or pseudonymous works must not be presented as verified apostolic authorship. New additions include scholarly research-source URLs. A source supports only the claims described in its entry; it does not automatically verify every textual or attribution statement.

records.date_precision: approximate; inferred from its reference before the extant 1 Corinthians; exact date unknown

records.later_canonical_compilation_status: not part of the later 27-writing collection; historical classification only

records.title: Paul's Sorrowful / Tearful Letter to Corinth
records.date_precision: approximate; placed between 1 Corinthians and the correspondence represented by 2 Corinthians; exact date debated
records.attribution_status: Paul refers to a letter written with distress and many tears; many scholars identify it as a separate lost letter, while some propose that material now in 2 Corinthians may preserve it.
records.textual_status: Not independently preserved as a complete identifiable writing. Possible identification with portions of 2 Corinthians 10–13 is disputed and must not be treated as established.
records.later_canonical_compilation_status: not part of the later 27-writing collection; historical classification only
records.chronology_basis: Relative sequence from 2 Corinthians 2:1–4 and 7:8–12; exact date and relationship to 2 Corinthians remain debated.

records.title: Epistle to Diognetus
records.date_precision: Most scholarship favors a later second-century date; exact date and authorship unknown
records.attribution_status: Anonymous. The claim that the author was a disciple of apostles is textually present but does not securely identify the author or prove direct apostolic association.
records.textual_status: Greek text survives in a single medieval manuscript that was later lost; modern editions depend on earlier copies/transcriptions. The physical witness date must not be mistaken for composition date.
records.later_canonical_compilation_status: not part of the later 27-writing collection; historical classification only
records.chronology_basis: Cambridge overview notes that most scholars favor a late-second-century date.

research_sources.title: Cambridge Companion to the Apostolic Fathers — dating overview

records.title: Martyrdom of Polycarp
records.date_precision: Second-century composition; exact date debated
records.attribution_status: An early account concerning Polycarp; its narrative and transmission must be evaluated as a historical source rather than treated as a verbatim eyewitness transcript.
records.textual_status: Survives in Greek manuscript transmission and later versions; manuscript witnesses are distinct from the date of composition.
records.later_canonical_compilation_status: not part of the later 27-writing collection; historical classification only
records.chronology_basis: Placed broadly in the second half of the second century; narrower dating remains disputed.

research_sources.title: Cambridge Companion to the Apostolic Fathers — dating overview

records.title: Acts of Andrew
records.date_precision: Late second to early third century; broad scholarly range
records.attribution_status: A later narrative about Andrew; not authenticated as a work written by the apostle.
records.textual_status: The original work is not fully extant; substantial portions are known through later summaries and versions. Do not present a later summary as the original manuscript text.
records.later_canonical_compilation_status: not part of the later 27-writing collection; historical classification only
records.chronology_basis: Oxford Reference dates the five earliest apocryphal Acts broadly to the late second through early third centuries; individual dating and textual histories remain distinct.

records.title: Acts of John

records.textual_status: Beginning is missing; surviving material is reconstructed from multiple manuscript and quotation sources. Fragmentary transmission must be shown explicitly.
records.later_canonical_compilation_status: not part of the later 27-writing collection; historical classification only
records.chronology_basis: Oxford Reference dates the five earliest apocryphal Acts broadly to the late second through early third centuries; individual dating and textual histories remain distinct.

records.title: Acts of Peter
records.date_precision: Late second to early third century; broad scholarly range
records.attribution_status: A later narrative attributed to Peter by its subject and tradition; not an authenticated composition by the apostle.
records.textual_status: The main narrative is preserved in Latin (Vercelli Acts); Greek witnesses preserve martyrdom material. Do not assume the surviving forms represent one complete identical text.
records.later_canonical_compilation_status: not part of the later 27-writing collection; historical classification only
records.chronology_basis: Oxford Reference dates the five earliest apocryphal Acts broadly to the late second through early third centuries; individual dating and textual histories remain distinct.

records.title: Correspondence of Paul and Seneca
records.date_precision: commonly regarded as a later, probably fourth-century pseudepigraphal correspondence; exact date uncertain
records.attribution_status: A collection of letters attributed to Paul and Seneca; not regarded as authentic correspondence from Paul's lifetime.
records.textual_status: Survives in Latin manuscript transmission; manuscript witnesses must be catalogued separately.
records.later_canonical_compilation_status: not part of the later 27-writing collection; historical classification only
records.chronology_basis: Date refers to the later composition of the pseudepigraphal correspondence.

records.title: Epistle to the Laodiceans (Latin work)
records.date_precision: broad provisional late-antique range; exact date and origin disputed
records.attribution_status: A later work presented under Paul's name; not established as an authentic letter written by Paul. Its identity with the letter mentioned in Colossians 4:16 is unproven.
records.textual_status: A Latin text survives in later manuscript transmission; it is not evidence that the lost Laodicean correspondence mentioned in Colossians has been recovered.
records.later_canonical_compilation_status: not part of the later 27-writing collection; historical classification only
records.chronology_basis: Provisional date for the surviving pseudepigraphal work, not the date of the correspondence mentioned in Colossians.

records.title: Letter to the Alexandrians (reported as a Pauline writing)
records.date_precision: Undated; no reliable composition date is established.
records.attribution_status: The Muratorian Fragment mentions a letter to the Alexandrians as forged in Paul's name; no authentic Pauline authorship is established.
records.textual_status: No securely identified complete text or manuscript witness; retained as an ancient report of an attributed/forged writing, not as a recovered Pauline letter.
records.later_canonical_compilation_status: not part of the later 27-writing collection; historical classification only
records.chronology_basis: The Muratorian Fragment reports a forged letter under Paul's name but does not provide a secure composition date. Unknown dates are sorted after dated records.
